then.text: Enjoy the coffee! Tell Bríd we said hello.

else.text: Brown sugar for Chef Bríd? Coming up. It's on the house: we owe Foynes, really. Shannon took over when the flying boats stopped.
You've got a bag of brown sugar for the Irish coffee.
Welcome to the world's first duty-free shop! Opened 1947. Whiskey, perfume, cheese, a remarkable number of leprechauns.

duty_free.text: Brendan O'Regan thought it up: let the transatlantic passengers buy without tax while the plane refuels. Now every airport has one. You're welcome, world.

airport_announcer.text: Shannon has US preclearance: you go through American immigration here, before you fly. You land in America like a domestic passenger. Very handy.
Before the jets, nearly every flight between Europe and North America stopped here for fuel. Shannon was the doorway to the New World. Now it's a doorway with a very good shop.

airport_child.text: I'm going to Boston to see my aunties! There are more Irish people in America than in Ireland, my da says. They all want to see me.
